title: Drop Interface
concept: The Drop interface provides a destructor — code that runs automatically when a value goes out of scope, ideal for resource cleanup.
why: Without Drop, you'd have to manually close files, free memory, and disconnect sockets. Drop automates cleanup — no leaks, no forgotten resources.
tips: Use Drop for ALL resource cleanup — files, sockets, locks, GPU buffers
Drop runs in ALL exit scenarios — normal, early return, or panic — it's guaranteed
Fields drop in reverse declaration order — put dependencies before dependants
Don't call drop() manually unless you have a specific reason — let the scope handle it
common_mistakes: Calling drop() manually and then using the value — it's been cleaned up
Assuming Drop runs when a value is moved — it runs when the original scope ends, not on move
Forgetting that Drop might panic — this can cause double-panic and abort during unwinding
